artists.biography: Monster Magnet is an American stoner rock band. Hailing from Red Bank, New Jersey, the group was founded by Dave Wyndorf (vocals and guitar), John McBain (guitar) and Tim Cronin (vocals and drums). The band first went by the names "Dog of Mystery", "Airport 75", "Triple Bad Acid" and "King Fuzz" before finally settling on "Monster Magnet", taken from the name of a 1960s toy made by Wham-O, which Wyndorf liked when he was a child.

perplexity.description:
4-Way Diablo" is the seventh studio album by American rock band Monster Magnet, originally released in November 2007. The album showcases the band's signature blend of stoner rock, psychedelic rock, and hard rock, characterized by heavy guitar riffs, spaced-out atmospheres, and frontman Dave Wyndorf's distinctive vocals. Recorded across four different studios—including the legendary Sound City Studios—the album features a dynamic range of sounds, from driving rock anthems to more experimental, groove-laden tracks, reflecting Monster Magnet's ability to merge classic rock influences with a modern, psychedelic edge.

Within Monster Magnet's discography, "4-Way Diablo" stands as a return to form after a period of lineup changes and stylistic experimentation. It reaffirms the band's reputation for crafting immersive, riff-heavy rock music, while also demonstrating a willingness to explore new sonic textures. The album received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised its energy, songwriting, and production, though it did not achieve major commercial success. Released under Napalm Records, "4-Way Diablo" remains a respected entry in the band's catalog and a solid example of their enduring influence in the rock genre.
